brief.studentFacingIntro: This self-study assessment asks you to demonstrate practical HRIS skills and secure data handling in a realistic UK HR context. You will: 1) explain the HR function, lifecycle stages and core HRIS data fields; 2) create a new starter in an HRIS sandbox applying UK data protection controls; and 3) carry out lifecycle updates using validation rules and provide audit evidence. All work must be completed independently using a publicly available HRIS demo, a free trial HRIS account, or the provided spreadsheet template if a sandbox is unavailable. Do not use any real personal data. Use only anonymised sample data.
brief.workplaceContext: You are the sole HR Administrator for a 120-employee UK SME. The Operations Director has requested evidence that the HR function understands the UK employee lifecycle and can maintain accurate, secure HR records. You are piloting a basic HRIS. You must: produce a concise briefing on HR foundations for leadership, create a compliant starter record for a new joiner in the HRIS sandbox, and demonstrate accurate lifecycle changes (e.g., probation confirmation and salary update) with validation rules and full audit history for internal assurance.
stepByStepInstructions: Select your tools: choose one HRIS demo or trial (e.g., a publicly available HRIS demo site) or use the provided spreadsheet-based HRIS template if you cannot access a demo. Ensure you can capture screenshots and export or show audit trails.
Plan anonymised sample data: create a fictional new starter and a current employee record for lifecycle updates. Do not use real names, NI numbers, or any identifiable data.

Part A – HR foundations briefing (MLO 1): outline the HR function in a UK SME, map the employee lifecycle stages (attraction, recruitment, onboarding, probation, changes, leave/absence, development, exit), and list core HRIS data fields required at each stage (e.g., name, date of birth, address, contact details, job title, department, start date, manager, employment type, right-to-work evidence status, NI number, bank details, emergency contact, working hours, salary, absence entitlements). Explain where and why each field is captured.

Part B – Onboarding in HRIS with data protection controls (MLO 2): in your HRIS sandbox, create the new starter record. Demonstrate at least four concrete controls aligned to UK GDPR (e.g., data minimisation by deferring bank details until payroll setup; field validation on NI number format; role-based access for sensitive fields; privacy notice link acknowledged; use of test data only; masking sensitive fields in evidence; recording lawful basis and retention category where available). Capture annotated screenshots and complete the provided Data Protection Controls Checklist.

Part C – Lifecycle updates with validation rules and audit trails (MLO 3): perform two lifecycle updates on the existing employee record (for example: 1) probation status change with effective date; 2) salary change with approval reference). Configure or demonstrate relevant validation (e.g., effective date cannot be in the past/future beyond policy, salary must be numeric within range, mandatory approver field). Export or capture the audit trail showing who made the change, when, and the before/after values. Include test evidence showing invalid data is rejected.

Record a screen walkthrough: produce an 8–10 minute narrated screen recording showing key steps in Parts B and C (no real data on screen). Clearly state the controls and validations you applied and point to the audit evidence.

Compile your portfolio: combine the briefing (Part A), annotated screenshots, completed checklist, validation test evidence, audit trail extracts, and a short reflection (how your controls meet UK GDPR principles in this context). Cross-reference all evidence to the steps above.

Self-check before submission: use the Pre-Submission Checklist to verify anonymisation, required controls, evidence of validation and audit trails, file naming, and that your video is viewable. Resolve any gaps before you submit.
Submit: upload a single ZIP containing your portfolio (PDF or DOCX) and your MP4 recording. Keep your original working files until grading is complete.
deliverables: Part A: HR Foundations briefing note covering HR function, lifecycle stages, and core HRIS data fields for UK organisations (MLO 1).
Part B: Evidence of onboarding starter creation with applied data protection controls in HRIS sandbox, including completed Data Protection Controls Checklist and annotated screenshots (MLO 2).
Part C: Evidence of two lifecycle updates with validation rules and audit trail extracts (before/after, user, timestamp) plus test evidence of rejected invalid entries (MLO 3).
Screen recording (8–10 minutes, narrated) demonstrating Parts B and C, highlighting controls, validations and audit logs.
Pre-Submission Checklist and Academic Integrity Declaration.

rubric.criterionName: HR function, lifecycle mapping, and core HRIS data fields (MLO 1)
rubric.fail: Description is inaccurate, overly generic, or missing key lifecycle stages. Core HRIS fields are largely omitted or incorrect; no clear linkage between fields and lifecycle stages.
rubric.pass: Accurate description of the HR function and main UK employee lifecycle stages. Identifies core HRIS fields for each stage with basic justification of why they are needed.
rubric.merit: Clear, well-structured description linking HR responsibilities to each lifecycle stage. Provides a coherent data field mapping with concise rationale reflecting UK practice and demonstrates understanding of dependencies between fields and stages.
rubric.distinction: Comprehensive and succinct description synthesising HR function with lifecycle flow. Presents a precise data field map that distinguishes mandatory vs conditional fields, aligns with UK terminology and good practice, and anticipates data quality risks at each stage.

rubric.criterionName: Application of data protection controls during onboarding in HRIS (MLO 2)
rubric.fail: Creates a starter record without demonstrable controls; evidence includes real personal data or lacks anonymisation. Cannot show how UK data protection principles are applied.
rubric.pass: Implements and evidences at least four relevant controls (e.g., data minimisation, field validation, role-based access, privacy notice acknowledgement, masking in evidence). Uses only anonymised sample data and completes the checklist.
rubric.merit: Controls are well-chosen, correctly configured, and clearly evidenced with annotations and brief justification of how each supports UK GDPR principles. No exposure of sensitive data in artefacts.
rubric.distinction: Controls are systematically planned and evidenced, covering prevention, detection, and user awareness (e.g., permissions, masked outputs, minimised capture, retention tags where available). Provides clear reasoning that maps controls to specific UK GDPR principles with zero leakage of sensitive data in all artefacts.

rubric.criterionName: Validation rules and audit trail evidence for lifecycle updates (MLO 3)
rubric.fail: Lifecycle updates are inaccurate or incomplete; no working validation is shown; audit history is missing or does not show who/when/what changed.
rubric.pass: Accurately performs two lifecycle updates with working validation preventing at least one type of invalid input. Provides audit evidence showing actor, timestamp, and before/after values.
rubric.merit: Validation rules are appropriate to the change types and are demonstrated with positive and negative tests. Audit evidence is clearly labelled and traceable to each update.
rubric.distinction: Validation comprehensively prevents common data errors (e.g., date ranges, formats, mandatory approvals) and is evidenced with systematic test cases. Audit trail is complete, clearly linked to policy, and demonstrates end-to-end traceability for each update.

rubric.criterionName: Portfolio quality, traceability and compliance of evidence (MLO 2, MLO 3)
rubric.fail: Portfolio is disorganised, missing required artefacts, or includes real personal data. Evidence cannot be traced to tasks.
rubric.pass: All required artefacts are present, clearly labelled, anonymised, and referenced to tasks. File naming and links are functional.
rubric.merit: Portfolio is logically structured with a contents list and cross-references from requirements to evidence. Self-check is completed with minor or no corrections required.
rubric.distinction: Portfolio demonstrates professional standards: consistent file naming and metadata, clear cross-referencing, explicit evidence map to MLOs and rubric, and a complete pre-submission checklist with corrective actions documented.

evidenceRequirements.additionalNotes: Use the provided Briefing Note Template; include a simple table mapping lifecycle stages to core HRIS fields.

evidenceRequirements.artefactType: Onboarding in HRIS with data protection controls (Part B)
evidenceRequirements.wordCountOrDuration: Up to 6 pages of annotated screenshots
evidenceRequirements.additionalNotes: Include completed Data Protection Controls Checklist (template provided) and clearly mask any sensitive fields in images.

evidenceRequirements.artefactType: Lifecycle updates: validation and audit trail pack (Part C)
evidenceRequirements.wordCountOrDuration: Up to 8 pages of test evidence and audit exports
evidenceRequirements.additionalNotes: Include validation rule settings (where visible), positive and negative test cases, and audit trail extracts showing actor, timestamp, and before/after values.

evidenceRequirements.artefactType: Screen recording of HRIS workflow (Parts B and C)
evidenceRequirements.additionalNotes: Narrate your steps and call out the specific controls, validations, and audit evidence. Ensure captions/subtitles are enabled or provide a transcript.

evidenceRequirements.artefactType: Pre-Submission Checklist and Academic Integrity Declaration
evidenceRequirements.additionalNotes: Use the provided checklist; sign and date the declaration.

self_study.academicIntegrity: You must complete this assessment independently. You may use publicly available digital resources (e.g., HRIS demo sites or trials, official guidance, vendor documentation, and the provided templates). You may use generative tools for planning, proofreading, or formatting only if you critically review and edit outputs; you must declare any such use. Prohibited: submitting work produced by another person; sharing or reusing another learner’s files; using real personal data (yours or others’) in any artefact; altering timestamps or audit logs; fabricating evidence. All data must be anonymised and fictional. By submitting, you confirm the work is your own, all sources and tools are acknowledged, and all evidence is genuine and collected by you in the stated environment.
self_study.accessibilityOptions: Reasonable adjustments are available without lowering academic standards. Alternatives include: 1) instead of a narrated video, submit annotated screenshots plus a written transcript (1,000–1,200 words) covering the same steps; 2) use the spreadsheet HRIS template if a web demo is not accessible; 3) submit materials in accessible formats (DOCX, tagged PDF) with descriptive alt text for images; 4) provide captions or a transcript for all audio. If you require extended time, larger fonts, high-contrast templates, or keyboard-only workflows, inform the programme team in advance. Assessment criteria and required learning outcomes remain the same for all variants.

brief.studentFacingIntro: This assignment demonstrates your ability to describe core HR foundations and apply data protection and accuracy controls inside an HR information system (HRIS). You will work in an HRIS sandbox to create compliant starter records using provided case data and to process common lifecycle updates with validation and audit evidence. Your submission is a concise portfolio of evidence. Hybrid options are provided so you can submit either annotated screenshots and a written narrative, or a short recorded walkthrough (or live demo) covering the same evidence.
brief.workplaceContext: You are the HR Coordinator in a UK organisation onboarding new starters into a cloud HRIS. Your HR Director expects you to describe how HR works across the employee lifecycle, identify the core HRIS fields your team must maintain, and show that you can create accurate starter records while protecting personal data. In week two, you are asked to process lifecycle changes (e.g., probation confirmation and a change in working hours) and to demonstrate that your updates are accurate, validated, and auditable.
stepByStepInstructions: Step 1: Review the provided case pack (two fictional new starters, role profiles, start dates, managers, work patterns, and pay data). Use only the synthetic data supplied.

Step 2: Outline the HR function and the employee lifecycle stages relevant to your context (e.g., attraction, onboarding, employment changes, offboarding). Identify how HR interacts with these stages.

Step 3: List the core HRIS data fields required for UK onboarding and ongoing lifecycle accuracy (e.g., legal name, address, NI number, date of birth, job title, FTE, department, manager, work location, start date, salary, right-to-work status). Indicate which are mandatory for a valid starter record in your sandbox.

Step 4: Prepare your data protection approach for onboarding: plan how you will minimise data entry to what is necessary, avoid storing copies of identity documents in the portfolio, redact sensitive values in screenshots (e.g., NI number), and use secure filenames.

Step 5: Create two starter records in the HRIS sandbox using the case pack. Apply data protection controls during entry (e.g., do not input unnecessary fields, check accuracy against the case data, avoid visible PII in any exported evidence).

Step 6: Document the controls you applied (e.g., redaction method, role-based access assumptions noted for the sandbox, secure storage approach for your working files, privacy notice acknowledgement step if present in the workflow).

Step 7: Apply validation rules when saving the starter records (e.g., mandatory fields completed, effective date logic, valid NI format if applicable, date of birth age reasonableness, manager exists). Record any system warnings and show how you resolved them.

Step 8: Process lifecycle updates for the same employees: at minimum, (a) confirm probation, (b) change working hours or FTE, and (c) change manager or job title. Use effective dating and check that downstream fields update consistently.
Step 9: Extract or capture the audit trail for each lifecycle change (e.g., audit log export or system screen showing user, timestamp, old vs new values). Annotate screenshots to highlight evidence.
Step 10: Compile a concise narrative (plain English) explaining how your validation checks and audit evidence show accuracy and traceability of changes.

Step 11: Assemble your portfolio. Choose one of the hybrid evidence pathways: (A) Written + annotated screenshots, or (B) 8–10 minute recorded walkthrough (or live demo) plus a shorter written summary. Ensure no real personal data is included.
Step 12: Check your submission against the rubric. Ensure redactions are applied, filenames are de-identified (e.g., CandidateA_Starter_Evidence.pdf), and all requested items are included.

brief.studentFacingIntro: This assessment simulates core recruitment logistics in a UK setting. You will prepare a concise summary of acceptable right-to-work (RTW) evidence, build and communicate an interview schedule that meets real availability constraints, and perform a live, invigilated RTW check using mock documents. Your submission must show accurate application of current Home Office guidance and sound coordination practices. All work is individual, with opportunities to rehearse steps in class before the marked practical.
brief.workplaceContext: You are an HR Coordinator at Ridgefield Services Ltd., supporting the hiring of three Customer Support Assistants. The Hiring Manager (Sophie Green) and a panel member (David Khan) must attend each interview. Interviews are 30 minutes, with a 10‑minute changeover. Rooms and availability are constrained, and at least one candidate prefers a virtual interview. After interviews, you must complete RTW checks for candidates moving to offer, recording outcomes using the organisation’s pre-employment checklist and storing records securely.
stepByStepInstructions: Preparation (before Week 2 workshop): Access the current UK Home Office employer right-to-work guidance. Note acceptable document categories, use of share codes/online checks, original vs. copy requirements, face-to-face vs. remote check rules, and follow-up check triggers.

Task A – RTW Evidence Summary (MLO 1): Create a two-page summary that lists main evidence types and clearly states validity rules (e.g., expiry/limitations, when online checks are required, circumstances requiring a follow-up check). Include a brief citation of the guidance version/date and links used.

Task B – Interview Scheduling (MLO 2): Using the scenario constraints below, produce an interview schedule, room bookings, and communications pack. Interviews are 30 minutes with 10 minutes changeover. Include calendar invites for the panel and candidates, a run sheet for the day, and a brief contingency plan for a late change.

Scheduling scenario resources: Panel availability: Sophie Green (Tue 09:30–12:30; Wed 15:00–17:00; Fri 10:00–12:00); David Khan (Tue 10:00–16:00; Thu 09:00–12:00). Rooms: Room 2.10 (Tue 10:00–12:00), Room 3.05 (Wed 15:00–17:00). Virtual platform: MS Teams available; create links for virtual interviews. Candidate availability and preferences: Emma Jones (Tue 10:00–11:00 or Thu 09:00–10:30; prefers virtual), Mark Chen (Tue 11:00–12:00 or Wed 16:00–17:00; in-person only), Aisha Patel (Thu 09:30–11:30; open to virtual or in-person).

Scheduling outputs: Provide (i) a final timetable with times, panel, room/link, and candidate; (ii) draft calendar invites (panel and candidate versions) including joining instructions, accessibility information, and contact details; (iii) a one-page contingency plan describing how you will handle one same-day change.

Task C – RTW Check Practical (MLO 3): In class, you will perform a live RTW check on two mock candidate document packs provided by the tutor. Follow current guidance to verify identity, document validity, and any restrictions. Complete the Pre-employment Checklist for each candidate during the practical. Create compliant copies/records as instructed.

Recording and storage (MLO 3): After the practical, finalise your checklists and compile redacted copies of checked documents as directed in class. Provide a one-page secure storage note describing where and how records will be stored (physical/digital location, access controls, encryption/password protection if digital, naming convention, and audit trail notes). Do not include real personal data.

Portfolio assembly and submission: Print and collate Task A, Task B outputs, and Task C documentation into a single portfolio. Include the signed authenticity declaration on the cover sheet provided in class. Bring the portfolio on the due date. The RTW check practical will be completed and observed in class; observation outcomes will be added to your assessor record.
deliverables: Task A: Right-to-Work Evidence Summary (two pages) citing current Home Office guidance
Task B: Interview Scheduling Pack (schedule workbook, run sheet, and draft calendar/email invites with room/link details and contingency plan)
Task C: Pre-employment Checklists (two candidates) with compliant copies/records as instructed, plus a one-page secure storage note

brief.studentFacingIntro: In this self-study simulation you will complete the core logistics of a UK recruitment process. brief.workplaceContext: You are an HR Coordinator at a mid-sized UK services company recruiting two Customer Support Associates. You must coordinate interviews across busy hiring managers, ensure rooms and virtual links are ready, and complete compliant RTW checks before issuing offers. The Head of HR has provided anonymised candidate profiles and sample RTW documents. Your outputs will be reviewed during an internal compliance audit.
stepByStepInstructions: Download the resource pack from the LMS: (a) Anonymised candidate availability and panel availability (CSV/PDF), (b) Interview Scheduling Workbook (XLSX) with workflow template, (c) Pre-employment Checklist (DOCX), (d) Sample RTW documents bundle (PDFs), (e) Secure Storage SOP and naming convention (PDF), (f) Self-check checklist (DOCX).

Part A — RTW Evidence Summary (MLO 1): Using current GOV.UK/Home Office employer guidance, produce a concise table that lists accepted RTW evidence types and validity rules. Include: document types, whether a document provides a continuous or time-limited right to work, required follow-up check intervals (if any), when to use the online RTW service or Employer Checking Service, and any restrictions that affect work (for example, limited hours). Include clickable hyperlinks to the exact GOV.UK pages you used and the date you accessed them.

Part B — Interview Scheduling Workflow (MLO 2): Use the Interview Scheduling Workbook to map your workflow from request to confirmed interview. Incorporate: panel coordination, room booking or virtual meeting creation, candidate availability constraints, buffer times, and confirmations. Complete the provided scheduling matrix to allocate interview slots that satisfy all constraints. Export example calendar invitations (or screenshots) for two confirmed interviews showing date/time, room or virtual link, attendees, and joining instructions. Include brief rationale for any trade-offs you made (e.g., when no perfect slot existed).

Part C — Execute Simulated RTW Checks (MLO 3): For two anonymised candidates in the pack, execute a simulated RTW check using the Pre-employment Checklist. For each candidate: (1) Review the supplied sample documents or online check evidence, (2) Record the outcome and any follow-up date in the checklist, (3) Generate a file name and storage path that follow the Secure Storage SOP, and (4) Draft a brief note describing how you would store the evidence securely (access controls, retention period, and audit trail). Do not include any real personal data beyond what is already anonymised in the pack.

Part D — Screen-Recorded Walkthrough: Create a 5–7 minute screen recording narrating: (1) your RTW summary structure and how you verified current guidance, (2) your scheduling workflow and how constraints were met, and (3) how you executed the RTW checks and will store records securely.

Self-check before submission: Use the provided self-check checklist to confirm that (a) all links to GOV.UK are working and dated, (b) all candidate and panel constraints are satisfied in the final schedule, (c) pre-employment checklists are fully completed with outcomes and (if relevant) follow-up dates, (d) secure storage naming and retention are specified, (e) the recording plays and is within duration, and (f) files are correctly named and accessible as PDFs/MP4.
Package your submission: Export written components to PDF or DOCX as specified, name files using the SOP convention, place all files in a single ZIP, and upload via the LMS.

brief.studentFacingIntro: In this in-person assessment you will create an onboarding communications pack, analyse onboarding feedback to propose day-one improvements, and build a realistic two-week induction schedule within resource constraints. You will submit a concise printed portfolio and deliver a short in-class briefing. The assignment mirrors typical HR administrator and coordinator tasks and will be assessed against the module learning outcomes.
brief.workplaceContext: You are the HR Coordinator for a UK-based SME (approx. 180 employees). Five new starters are joining next Monday across IT, Finance, and Customer Support. You must prepare inclusive joining instructions, improve the day-one experience based on recent onboarding survey responses and FAQs, and create a two-week induction schedule that fits resource constraints. Constraints and resources: • Working hours 09:30–17:30; 60-minute lunch taken between 12:30–14:00. • One IT technician available for account setup in 45-minute slots; capacity: 2 slots per day. • Mandatory e-learning due in week one: Health & Safety (60 mins), Data Protection (45 mins), Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (45 mins). • Face-to-face sessions with limited availability: HR policy briefing (30 mins, Mon/Tue only), Manager 1:1 (30 mins, Wed–Fri only), Department tour (20 mins, any day), Team introductions (30 mins, any day, PM only), Facilities induction (20 mins, Mon/Wed only). • Equipment collection (20 mins) and building access set-up (15 mins) handled by Facilities. • Two small meeting rooms (max 6 people) and one induction room (max 12 people). • New starter day one arrival at 09:45; security pass collection at reception before 10:15.
stepByStepInstructions: Step 1: Review the workplace context, timings, and capacity constraints provided in class, including the onboarding survey dataset and FAQs pack.
Step 2: Sketch a high-level two-week onboarding plan for one new starter role of your choice (IT, Finance, or Customer Support) to act as the basis for communications and scheduling.

Step 3: Draft inclusive joining instructions and a clear day-one agenda aligned to your two-week plan. Ensure tone, accessibility, and practical details (time, location, contacts, what to bring) are correct.
Step 4: Analyse the provided onboarding survey responses and FAQs to identify key pain points for day one. Quantify findings where possible (counts, themes, frequency).

Step 5: Prioritise the top three day-one improvements using evidence from your analysis. Justify choices with a brief rationale that references the data and expected impact on the new starter experience.
Step 6: Integrate the three improvements into the day-one agenda and adjust the two-week plan as needed while staying within resource constraints.
Step 7: Build a detailed two-week induction schedule (table or Gantt) that coordinates mandatory training, IT setup, introductions, facilities, and manager availability within the given constraints.
Step 8: Prepare a concise in-class briefing (6–8 minutes) summarising your communications approach, top three improvements and rationale, and how your schedule meets constraints.
Step 9: Bring a printed copy of your portfolio to class for submission and deliver your briefing. Upload electronic copies to the LMS within 24 hours.
deliverables: Joining instructions email and day-one agenda aligned to the two-week plan.
Two-week induction schedule (table or Gantt) that respects stated constraints.

brief.workplaceContext: You are an HR Operations Administrator in a UK organisation with a monthly payroll. The payroll cut-off is at 12:00 on the 25th of the month. You receive a pack of instructions and anonymised employee data for: one new starter (mid-month), one existing employee with contractual changes (hours and pay rate), and one leaver (final pay in month). You must compile the cut-off pack with required evidence, calculate statutory leave entitlements and holiday pay for a set of typical scenarios (including part-time and pro-rata cases), and analyse the monthly payroll and absence variance reports to correct any inconsistencies before final submission to payroll.
stepByStepInstructions: Collect your anonymised case pack in class (starter, change, leaver, and leave/absence scenarios), the payroll calendar, and the organisation’s policy extracts and templates provided by the assessor.

Complete the Payroll Cut-off Checklist for the month. For each case (starter, change, leaver), populate the correct form/template and attach the required evidence (e.g., signed contract/variation letter, starter details, leave form, termination confirmation) using the Evidence Log template. Ensure dates align with the cut-off.
For the starter: apply the correct start date, pay basis, and any pro-rated elements. Note any implications for first pay (e.g., prorated salary, holiday accrual start).
For the contractual change: update hours/pay rate effective date and calculate any part-month adjustments if applicable. Record justification and attach the signed change documentation.
For the leaver: apply correct leave date and final pay components per the scenario (e.g., outstanding holiday pay, deductions if any). Ensure correct calculation approach is documented and evidenced.

Calculate statutory leave entitlements and holiday pay for the provided UK scenarios, including part-time and mid-year starter cases. Use the Leave Calculator template; show your working and cite policy or statutory basis where relevant.

Review the provided payroll and absence variance reports (this month versus last and plan). Identify anomalies (e.g., unexpected pay changes, missing absence data, misaligned hours) and record them on the Variance Analysis template with proposed corrections and rationale.

Apply and document corrections in your pack: update figures, annotate the source of truth, and produce a revised summary for submission. Ensure the audit trail is clear (before/after values, dates, and who authorised changes).

Prepare a concise Submission Cover Sheet listing all included items and a one-paragraph declaration that the work is your own. Assemble your printed portfolio in the order specified under Deliverables.

Attend the invigilated session to complete a short live check: you will be asked to reproduce one calculation and to explain your variance prioritisation. Deliver a 5-minute verbal walkthrough of your approach and key decisions, followed by brief questions.

Variance Analysis and Corrections: completed variance analysis template highlighting issues, impact, and corrective actions; revised figures where applicable.

brief.workplaceContext: You are the HR Operations Assistant for a UK organisation with a single monthly payroll and a mix of full-time, part-time, and variable-hours staff. stepByStepInstructions: 1. Access the assessment case pack: Obtain the starter/change/leaver case files, HRIS extracts, policy snippets, and prior/current month payroll and absence reports from your tutor (download from LMS or collect a printed pack).
2. Plan the cut-off: Note the cut-off date in the case pack. Create a task list to ensure all starters, changes, and leavers are captured with required approvals and evidence before cut-off.

3. Process starters, changes, and leavers (MLO 1): For each case, confirm effective dates align with cut-off rules; complete the payroll input workbook tabs; compile an evidence index referencing each source document (e.g., signed contract/offer or change form, approved pay change, resignation confirmation, final timesheet/holiday balance on exit); record any assumptions in an audit note.

6. Analyse payroll and absence variances (MLO 3): Compare the provided prior month and current draft reports. 9. Summarise key risks and decisions: Prepare either a 1‑page executive summary (PDF) or a 5‑minute presentation (live or recorded) outlining: main variances found, corrections made, and any residual risks or assumptions to flag to the payroll bureau.

brief.workplaceContext: You have joined a UK-based SME (250 employees) as an HR Coordinator. The company has implemented a new HRIS for onboarding new starters. stepByStepInstructions: Step 1: Attend the in-class workshop to review the provided onboarding process description and HRIS screenshots. Ask clarifying questions about actors, systems, documents and data fields involved.

Step 2: Draft an end-to-end onboarding data flow (from offer acceptance to Day 1) identifying data items, data subjects, systems, processors, transfer points and storage locations. Use the provided data flow template or your own tool.

Step 3: Analyse the data flow to identify GDPR risks (e.g. excessive collection, insecure transfer, unclear lawful basis, retention gaps, third-party processor risks, special category data handling). Rate likelihood and impact. Propose privacy-by-design mitigations that are specific and actionable (e.g. role-based access, secure portal uploads, data minimisation, encryption, retention rules, record of processing, approval checkpoints).

Step 4: Complete the policy register using the provided template. Include at least six current or draft policies (must include Disciplinary and Grievance) with fields populated (title, owner, author, approver, version, status, publication date, next review date, location/link, change summary, related legislation).

Step 5: Apply consistent policy naming conventions to two sample policy documents (Disciplinary and Grievance). Include a version control cover sheet/change log that demonstrates an auditable history (e.g. version number, date, author, approver, change notes).

Step 6: Using the provided sample Disciplinary and Grievance policies, analyse alignment with UK legal requirements. Identify concrete compliance gaps, risks and recommended actions (e.g. update steps, timelines, right to be accompanied, appeal routes, record-keeping). Prioritise actions and assign suggested owners and target dates.

Step 7: Compile your findings into a concise analytical report that integrates: (a) the data flow analysis, risks and mitigations; and (b) the disciplinary and grievance policy gap analysis with an action plan.

Step 8: Prepare 5–7 presentation slides summarising your key findings and recommendations. Present in class (8–10 minutes) followed by Q&A (up to 3 minutes). Use plain English suitable for non-technical stakeholders.
Step 9: Bring printed copies of your data flow diagram and action plan to the session for discussion. After the session, upload all required files to the LMS by the deadline.
Step 10: Complete the declaration of authenticity confirming the work is your own.
deliverables: Analytical report integrating GDPR data flow risk analysis with privacy-by-design mitigations, and a disciplinary/grievance policy gap analysis with action plan.
One-page onboarding HRIS data flow diagram with risk annotations or clear cross-reference to the report.
Policy version control pack: completed policy register (minimum six entries), two sample policy front pages with version control metadata, and files named using the agreed convention.
Presentation slides (5–7 slides) for in-class delivery.

brief.studentFacingIntro: This self-directed assignment simulates a realistic HR compliance task for a UK employer. You will analyse HRIS onboarding data flows for GDPR risks, implement policy version control that provides an auditable history, and review disciplinary and grievance policies against UK legal requirements to identify gaps and actions. You will compile your findings into a concise portfolio and record a short presentation summarising your approach and outcomes.
brief.workplaceContext: You are the HR Coordinator at a UK-based SME (approx. 120 employees) rolling out a new HR Information System (HRIS) for onboarding. The HR Director wants assurance that onboarding data flows comply with GDPR, that all HR policies are under version control for an upcoming audit, and that the disciplinary and grievance policies align with the ACAS Code of Practice and UK legal requirements. There is no budget for consultants, so you must deliver evidence the auditor can verify quickly.
stepByStepInstructions: Download or prepare the artefact workspace: create a folder with subfolders: 1_Data_Flows, 2_Policy_Register, 3_Compliance_Review, 4_Presentation.
Task A – Map onboarding HRIS data flows (MLO 1):
- Identify all onboarding data touchpoints: application-to-offer, pre-employment checks, contract issue, payroll setup, right-to-work evidence, induction scheduling, and system provisioning.
- Create a data flow diagram showing: data items collected, sources, systems/processors (including third parties), storage locations, transfers, access roles, retention/deletion points.

- Produce a GDPR risk analysis (DPIA-lite): list risks, likelihood/impact ratings, affected data subjects, lawful bases if relevant, and privacy-by-design mitigations. Prioritise actions and note residual risk.

Self-check A: Does your diagram show collection, storage, use, sharing, retention, and deletion? Have you flagged special category data, external processors, and access controls? Are mitigations specific and testable?
Task B – Implement policy version control (MLO 2):

- Build a policy register (spreadsheet) with, as a minimum: unique ID, policy title, owner, approver, version number, effective date, next review date, related documents, change summary, location/link.
- Define and document naming conventions for files (e.g., Department_PolicyName_vMajor.Minor_YYYYMMDD_Status).

- Apply the conventions to at least two HR policies (disciplinary and grievance): prepare current versions and archive a previous version or dummy prior state. Maintain a concise change log that explains what changed and why.
- Ensure your register and artefacts demonstrate an auditable history (e.g., version history screenshots or notes on where version history is maintained if using a cloud platform).
Self-check B: Are names consistent with your convention? Can an auditor trace a register entry to the exact file version and see what changed, when, and who approved it?
Task C – Analyse legal compliance for disciplinary and grievance policies (MLO 3):

- Review the current disciplinary and grievance policies against UK legal requirements, including the ACAS Code of Practice and relevant statutory requirements (e.g., right to be accompanied, fair procedure, reasonable timescales, appeal rights).
- Prepare a structured gap analysis with citations to the ACAS Code and legislation where applicable. Identify non-compliances, risks, and remedial actions.
- Provide a prioritised action plan with owners and target dates.
Self-check C: Have you referenced authoritative UK sources? Are your gaps specific (clause-level) and your actions practical and time-bound?
Task D – Record a short presentation:
- In 6–8 minutes, explain your data flow analysis and key risks, your privacy-by-design mitigations, how your version control system works, and the top compliance gaps and actions for the policies.
- Ensure clear audio, on-screen titles, and include captions or provide a transcript.
Final pre-submission checks:
- All documents are anonymised (no real employee data).
- File types are accessible (PDF/DOCX/XLSX/MP4) and named using your convention.
- Spelling, grammar, and referencing checked; export narrative documents to PDF.
- Complete the academic integrity declaration.
deliverables: Data flow diagram of onboarding HRIS processes (PDF or PNG) with legend and version label.
GDPR DPIA-lite risk analysis report with proposed privacy-by-design mitigations and prioritisation (PDF/DOCX).
Policy register spreadsheet showing version control fields and links/locations (XLSX/CSV).
Two policy documents (disciplinary and grievance) demonstrating version control, naming conventions, and change logs (PDF/DOCX).
Compliance gap analysis report for disciplinary and grievance policies with cited sources and action plan (PDF/DOCX).
Recorded presentation summarising approach and findings with captions or transcript (MP4 plus SRT or DOCX transcript).

brief.studentFacingIntro: This applied portfolio assesses your ability to protect employee data, maintain auditable policy documentation, and ensure disciplinary and grievance procedures comply with UK law. You will analyse HRIS onboarding data flows for GDPR risks and propose privacy-by-design mitigations, set up policy version control that stands up to audit, and review disciplinary and grievance policies to identify compliance gaps and required actions. The assessment is designed for hybrid delivery and can be completed using either your workplace (with anonymisation) or the provided case study.
brief.workplaceContext: You are an HR Coordinator in a UK SME implementing a new HRIS onboarding module ahead of an external audit. The HR Director requires: 1) a clear view of how onboarding data flows and where GDPR risks arise, with practical privacy-by-design mitigations; 2) a policy version control system to demonstrate an auditable history for HR policies; and 3) a compliance review of disciplinary and grievance policies against UK legal requirements to inform immediate improvements.
stepByStepInstructions: Select your context: either your current or recent employer (anonymised) or the provided UK SME case materials on the LMS. If using a real workplace, remove/obscure personal data and commercially sensitive information.

Scope onboarding: list the data fields collected during onboarding (e.g., identity, right-to-work, emergency contacts, bank details), the collection points, and the lawful bases used. Identify systems, vendors, and teams involved.

Map the data flow: produce an end-to-end onboarding data flow diagram showing inputs, systems, transfers (including any third-country processing), storage locations, access roles, and retention or deletion triggers.

Analyse GDPR risks: assess the mapped flows against GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 principles (lawfulness, fairness, transparency, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality, accountability). Identify specific risks, their likelihood/impact, and evidence (e.g., policy gaps, uncontrolled access, missing retention rules).

Propose privacy-by-design mitigations: for each material risk, specify practical controls (e.g., minimised data fields, role-based access, encryption, pseudonymisation, retention automation, DPIA triggers, vendor due diligence, secure transfer protocols) and show how these reduce risk.

Set up policy version control: create a policy register with fields such as Policy ID, title, owner, approver, version, status, effective date, review date, related documents, change summary, and link to source file. Define and apply a naming convention and standardised policy template with version headers and change logs.

Populate the register: add at least 8 HR policy entries including Disciplinary Policy and Grievance Policy. For at least 2 policies, include a demonstrable version history (minimum 3 versions) with dated change summaries and approvals.

Review disciplinary and grievance policies: analyse them against UK legal requirements and the Acas Code of Practice on Disciplinary and Grievance Procedures. Identify compliance gaps, risks, and recommended actions with priorities and realistic timelines.
Prepare a concise presentation (live or recorded): summarise your data flow risks and key mitigations, your version control approach, and the top 3 compliance gaps with actions.

Compile and submit: assemble your portfolio report with appendices (diagram, logs, register), your policy templates, and your presentation link/file via the LMS. If submitting physically, provide a printed pack and a USB drive with digital files.
deliverables: Onboarding data flow analysis pack: narrative analysis with references to GDPR principles; a data flow diagram; a risk and mitigation log.
Privacy-by-design summary: a short rationale explaining how proposed mitigations embed privacy by design and, where applicable, when to trigger a DPIA.
Policy version control pack: populated policy register, documented naming convention, and at least two policy templates showing version headers and change logs.
Disciplinary and grievance compliance review: a gap analysis with evidence, risk rating, and prioritised action plan.
Presentation (live or recorded): 5–7 minutes summarising findings and actions.

rubric.merit: Produces an accurate end-to-end data flow including access roles, retention/deletion points, and any third-country transfers. Analyses risks with clear likelihood and impact reasoning, explicitly referencing GDPR principles and lawful bases. Proposes targeted, practical privacy-by-design mitigations with justification.
rubric.distinction: Produces a comprehensive, precise data flow map covering inputs, processing, storage, access control, vendor touchpoints, special category data handling, and cross-border flows. Delivers a rigorous risk analysis that triangulates evidence (policy, system settings, vendor terms), prioritises risks, and explicitly maps each to GDPR principles and accountability obligations. Proposes an integrated, actionable set of privacy-by-design mitigations (technical, organisational, and process controls) with a clear rationale, implementation sequencing, and DPIA trigger criteria.

rubric.merit: Provides a structured analysis cross-referencing UK legal requirements and the Acas Code, covering procedural fairness, investigation, right to be accompanied, timeframes, confidentiality, and appeal. Presents a prioritised action plan with timescales and responsibilities.
rubric.distinction: Delivers a rigorous, evidence-based analysis aligned to UK legal requirements and the Acas Code, testing the policies for proportionality, clarity, accessibility, and equality implications. Clearly flags material compliance risks and operational impacts. brief.studentFacingIntro: This in-person assignment asks you to produce a working HR dashboard, a concise governance review, and a feasible automation plan. You will work with an anonymised HR dataset during scheduled labs and present your findings live. Your portfolio will demonstrate your ability to analyse core HR metrics (turnover, absence, pipeline), evaluate data governance, and apply report automation for monthly updates.
brief.workplaceContext: You are supporting the HR Manager in a UK organisation of 350 employees. The Executive Team has requested a monthly HR metrics pack. Current reports are manual and inconsistent. You have been asked to: 1) produce a dashboard that clearly shows turnover, absence, and recruitment pipeline trends; 2) evaluate data definitions, sources, and quality with stakeholders and recommend governance improvements; and 3) design a repeatable monthly automation approach with commentary and a clear distribution list.
stepByStepInstructions: Attend the in-class dataset briefing and sign the data handling agreement. Download the provided anonymised HR data (people, leavers, absence, and recruitment pipeline).
Define the required metrics in your notes: turnover rate, absence rate, and pipeline movement. State the exact formulas/logic you will use and any time windows (e.g., last 12 months).
Explore and prepare the data in your chosen tool (e.g., Excel/Power Query or Power BI). Identify and log data quality issues (e.g., missing dates, inconsistent job titles).

Build the dashboard: include visuals that show monthly trends for turnover, absence, and pipeline, with basic segmentation (e.g., department or location). Provide clear labels, filters/slicers, and an executive summary area.
Write narrative insights linked directly to your visuals. Identify at least three trend-based findings and at least two actionable implications for HR operations.

Evaluate data governance: document current data definitions and sources; assess quality (accuracy, completeness, timeliness, consistency). Draft a short data dictionary for key fields and note ownership, refresh frequency, and access controls.
Engage with stakeholders: participate in the in-class stakeholder clinic (role-play). Capture feedback, questions, or risks and refine your recommendations accordingly.

Design an automation approach for monthly updates: outline the end-to-end refresh steps, schedule, data checks, commentary capture process, and a distribution list with roles/permissions. If available, demonstrate a scheduled refresh or a mock run and include screenshots.

Prepare and deliver an 8–10 minute in-class presentation covering your dashboard walkthrough, key insights, governance findings, and automation plan. Bring a printed one-page dashboard handout for the audience.

Submit your portfolio files to the LMS by the deadline: dashboard file, narrative insights, governance review with data dictionary, automation plan with evidence of a test run (or detailed steps if scheduling tools are unavailable), slides, and distribution list.
deliverables: HR metrics dashboard file showing turnover, absence, and pipeline trends with filters and labels.
Narrative insights (executive summary) explicitly tied to dashboard visuals and trends.
Data governance review including data definitions, source mapping, quality assessment, and prioritised recommendations informed by stakeholder input.
Data dictionary for key HR fields used in the dashboard (concise table).
Report automation plan with schedule, steps, toolchain, commentary capture process, exception handling, and distribution list.
Presentation slides (8–10 minutes) and a printed one-page dashboard handout for the audience.

rubric.criterionName: Dashboard analysis and narrative insights (turnover, absence, pipeline)
rubric.fail: Metrics are missing or incorrectly calculated; visuals are unclear or do not show trends; no meaningful segmentation; narrative absent or not supported by the data; file does not run or contains major errors.
rubric.pass: Correctly calculates and displays turnover, absence, and pipeline trends over time; includes basic segmentation and clear labelling; provides a coherent narrative that identifies at least three trend-based insights and at least one practical action, all supported by visuals.
rubric.merit: Accurate, well-structured dashboard with useful filters and comparisons (e.g., department/location); interprets drivers of change and seasonal patterns; narrative connects insights to operational implications and limitations; design is consistent and readable; basic QA checks are evident.
rubric.distinction: Insight-rich analysis that highlights trends, outliers, and likely drivers using appropriate comparisons; narrative prioritises actions aligned to business impact and acknowledges data limitations; dashboard offers intuitive interaction (e.g., drill, slicers) and professional design conventions; steps are documented for reproducibility.

rubric.criterionName: Data definitions, sources, quality evaluation, and governance recommendations
rubric.fail: Superficial or inaccurate treatment of data definitions and sources; quality issues are not identified; recommendations are missing, generic, or not feasible; no evidence of stakeholder consideration.
rubric.pass: States clear working definitions for key metrics and fields; maps main data sources; identifies material quality issues (e.g., missing values, timing lags) with examples; proposes feasible recommendations addressing ownership, quality checks, and access; references stakeholder feedback.
rubric.merit: Evaluates definitions and sources with justification; assesses quality across accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and consistency with specific evidence; provides a concise data dictionary; recommendations are prioritised with expected benefits and effort; integrates stakeholder perspectives to refine proposals.
rubric.distinction: Provides a robust evaluation including data lineage and risks; articulates governance roles (e.g., ownership, stewardship), refresh cadence, and controls aligned to UK HR data protection expectations; presents a practical improvement roadmap with success measures; stakeholder engagement clearly informs final, prioritised recommendations.

rubric.criterionName: Report automation, monthly scheduling, commentary, and distribution
rubric.fail: No viable automation approach; schedule absent or unrealistic; commentary process not defined; distribution list missing or inappropriate; no evidence of testing or documentation.
rubric.pass: Outlines a feasible monthly automation approach with clear steps and timing; defines how commentary will be captured/updated; provides an appropriate distribution list with roles; includes basic evidence of a test run or detailed procedural steps.
rubric.merit: Implements or convincingly specifies a repeatable workflow with validation checks, error handling, and required permissions; provides a commentary template and ownership; tests a sample refresh or illustrates tool configuration with screenshots; distribution list aligns to reporting needs and confidentiality.
rubric.distinction: Demonstrates an efficient, low-risk automation design with monitoring, exception handling, and recovery steps; schedules are documented with prerequisites and dependencies; provides evidence of a successful test or mock run and change-log approach; commentary process and distribution governance are fully defined (recipients, cadence, access controls).

evidenceRequirements.artefactType: HR dashboard file (turnover, absence, pipeline) with filters and annotations
evidenceRequirements.fileType: XLSX or PBIX (plus any linked CSV files)
evidenceRequirements.additionalNotes: Ensure file paths are portable; include a brief readme with tool version and refresh steps.

evidenceRequirements.artefactType: Narrative insights (executive summary) aligned to visuals
evidenceRequirements.additionalNotes: Use clear headings; directly reference specific visuals (e.g., Figure 1).

evidenceRequirements.artefactType: Data governance review and recommendations with data dictionary
evidenceRequirements.fileType: PDF or DOCX (dictionary may be XLSX/CSV)
evidenceRequirements.additionalNotes: Include definitions, sources, quality assessment, ownership, refresh frequency, and prioritised actions.

evidenceRequirements.artefactType: Report automation plan with schedule, commentary process, and distribution list
evidenceRequirements.fileType: PDF or DOCX; images PNG/JPG embedded
evidenceRequirements.additionalNotes: If scheduling is demonstrated, include screenshots of the configuration or a mock run output.

evidenceRequirements.fileType: PPTX or PDF for slides; printed one-page dashboard handout
evidenceRequirements.additionalNotes: Bring a printed A4 dashboard summary for the audience; be prepared for 2–3 minutes of Q&A.

in_person.academicIntegrity: You must produce original work for this assignment. Collaboration in scheduled workshops and peer discussion is encouraged, but all analysis, writing, and files submitted must be your own. You may use standard software tools (e.g., Excel, Power Query, Power BI) and class-provided templates with acknowledgement. You must: cite any external templates, formulas, or design patterns used; keep a simple log of sources (web pages, articles) that informed your definitions or methods; and submit only files you have created. Prohibited conduct includes: copying another learner’s work; sharing your files for others to submit; allowing others to complete analysis or writing on your behalf; fabricating or altering data; and using generative AI to produce analysis, insights, recommendations, or graphics presented as your own. Generative AI may be used only for proofreading or formatting support with a brief disclosure note if used. You will be required to sign a declaration of authenticity at submission and may be invited to a short viva to verify your understanding.
in_person.accessibilityOptions: Reasonable adjustments are available without lowering academic standards. Options may include: extended time for the live presentation or an alternative scheduled slot; the ability to submit a recorded presentation if a disability or health condition prevents live delivery; alternative document formats (large print, high-contrast, structured templates); permission to use assistive technologies; accessible room setup for presentation and lab work; and alternative but equivalent evidence (e.g., oral explanation of governance findings in place of longer written text) where this fairly assesses the same learning outcomes. Requests should be made through the institution’s disability support service in advance, and agreed adjustments will be documented. All adjusted assessments will be marked to the same criteria.

brief.studentFacingIntro: This self-study portfolio assesses your ability to build an HR metrics dashboard, evaluate data governance, and set up a practical automation approach for monthly HR reporting. You will work with a provided sample dataset (or your own simulated data using the provided template) to calculate and visualise turnover, absence, and recruitment pipeline trends. You will also appraise data definitions, sources, and quality, and propose governance improvements with stakeholders. Finally, you will design and demonstrate an automation workflow that updates metrics monthly, includes commentary, and distributes outputs to a defined audience. All work must be completed independently and submitted digitally.
brief.workplaceContext: You are an HR Coordinator/Analyst in a UK-based organisation preparing a monthly People Metrics Pack for department heads. Data exports come from HRIS, ATS, and time/attendance systems. Leaders expect a clear dashboard on turnover, absence, and recruitment pipeline trends, with short written insights. Your HR Director has asked you to review data definitions and quality issues, and to recommend practical data governance improvements with named stakeholders. To reduce manual effort, you must implement or clearly evidence a repeatable automation plan that refreshes the data monthly, generates commentary, and distributes the pack to a defined mailing list.
stepByStepInstructions: Download the provided HR metrics data template (CSV/XLSX) from the LMS. Option A: Use the provided anonymised sample dataset. Option B: Simulate your own data in the same template structure (include realistic dates and values).

Create a data dictionary defining each field used (e.g., employee ID, start date, termination date, absence hours, pipeline stage dates). Include definition, format, source system, and any transformation rules.
Prepare the dataset for analysis. Clean missing values, normalise date formats, de-duplicate records, and document any assumptions. Keep a brief change log of data cleaning steps.

Calculate monthly metrics: a) Turnover (overall and voluntary where possible), b) Absence (e.g., absence rate or days lost per FTE), c) Recruitment pipeline (applications-to-offer and offer-to-accept conversion, time-in-stage or time-to-fill where possible). Show working or formulas.

Build a dashboard that highlights trends over time for turnover, absence, and pipeline. Include at least: time-series charts, a KPI summary tile for the latest month, and optional segment filters (e.g., department or location) if available.
Write concise narrative insights (bullet points) for each metric, highlighting notable changes, patterns, or risks. Include at least one actionable recommendation per metric.

Evaluate data definitions, sources, and quality. Identify gaps, duplicates, timeliness issues, or inconsistencies across HRIS/ATS/absence data. Prioritise the top 3–5 issues with evidence (examples or screenshots).

Recommend data governance improvements with stakeholders. Propose realistic actions (e.g., data ownership, access controls, validation rules at entry, data refresh cadence, retention/archiving, change control). Assign responsible roles or teams and an implementation timeline.

Design an automation approach that can run monthly with minimal manual effort using accessible tools (e.g., Google Sheets + Looker Studio, Excel + Power Query, or CSV refresh + scripted distribution). Specify the trigger (e.g., first business day), data refresh steps, and output generation.

Implement and evidence the automation: set up a scheduled refresh OR, if scheduling is not available, provide a reproducible manual refresh procedure with screenshots and timing notes. Include distribution list management (who receives what, how privacy is protected) and a short commentary template to be updated each month.
Test the end-to-end process using the current dataset. Capture before/after screenshots or a short log showing a successful refresh and output creation. Note any failure points and mitigations.
Record a 6–8 minute screen walkthrough (MP4) showing: the dashboard, how metrics are calculated, key insights, and how the monthly refresh/distribution is performed.

Compile your portfolio: a) PDF report including dashboard screenshots, KPI table for the latest month, narrative insights, data dictionary, governance evaluation, and recommendations; b) attach source data files; c) include automation plan, evidence of scheduling/refresh, and sample distribution list.

Complete the self-check before submission: validate metric formulas against the checker in the template (if using the provided dataset), confirm charts display correctly for at least two months, ensure governance recommendations are specific and assigned to stakeholders, and verify the recording plays with clear audio or a transcript.
Submit all items via the LMS in the required formats. Ensure filenames include your candidate ID and module code.
deliverables: PDF portfolio/report including: dashboard screenshots, KPI summary for the latest month, narrative insights, data dictionary, governance evaluation, and governance recommendations with stakeholders
Data files: cleaned dataset(s) used for analysis (CSV or XLSX) plus any transformation/Power Query files or SQL/automation scripts (if applicable)
Automation pack: written automation plan (including schedule, trigger, steps, distribution list, and commentary template) and evidence of configuration (screenshots/logs or export of settings)
MP4 screen recording (6–8 minutes) demonstrating the dashboard, calculations, insights, and refresh/distribution process
Optional read-only link to the interactive dashboard (if hosted online) with access restricted to marker emails (do not expose personal data)

rubric.criterionName: Dashboard analysis and insight (Turnover, Absence, Pipeline)
rubric.fail: Metrics are incomplete or incorrectly calculated; visuals are unclear or misleading; trends for turnover, absence, and pipeline are missing or not interpretable; minimal or no narrative insights.
rubric.pass: Correctly calculates and displays core turnover, absence, and pipeline metrics over time; charts are readable; provides basic, accurate narrative insights highlighting obvious changes.
rubric.merit: Provides accurate calculations with appropriate formulas and time windows; dashboard offers useful segmentation and comparative views; narrative insights interpret patterns and likely drivers with clear implications for action.
rubric.distinction: Shows rigorous analysis (e.g., trendlines, seasonality or cohort/segment comparisons, stage conversion and time metrics) with consistently accurate calculations; synthesises findings into concise, high-value insights with quantified impacts and prioritised actions; dashboard is well-structured, consistent, and decision-ready.

rubric.criterionName: Data definitions, sources and quality governance evaluation
rubric.fail: Data definitions are vague or missing; sources not identified; no systematic assessment of quality; governance recommendations are absent or generic and lack stakeholder ownership.
rubric.pass: Defines key terms and identifies main sources; flags obvious data quality issues (e.g., missing, duplicates, timeliness); provides feasible governance recommendations with named stakeholders at a basic level.
rubric.merit: Supplies a clear data dictionary with lineage from sources and transformation notes; evaluates quality across dimensions (accuracy, completeness, timeliness, consistency) using examples; proposes targeted governance improvements (ownership, access, validation rules, refresh cadence, retention) with roles and timeframes.
rubric.distinction: Presents a comprehensive evaluation connecting definitions, sources, and real data issues to root causes; prioritises improvements with effort/impact rationale; outlines an implementable governance model (roles, controls, monitoring, change control) with a stakeholder engagement plan and measurable success criteria.

rubric.criterionName: Report automation setup and scheduling with commentary and distribution
rubric.fail: No credible automation approach or evidence; schedule and distribution are missing; commentary not addressed.
rubric.pass: Outlines and evidences a workable monthly refresh approach (scheduled or reproducible manual), includes a distribution list and simple commentary template; provides basic screenshots or logs.
rubric.merit: Implements a reliable refresh/export with clear steps and audit evidence; parameterises for month-end; integrates a commentary template; defines recipients and privacy-safe distribution with testing evidence.
rubric.distinction: Demonstrates an end-to-end, low-effort automation using accessible tools; includes robust scheduling (or well-defined fallback), versioning/logging, validation checks, and privacy-aware distribution lists; supplies a concise SOP enabling another user to run the process successfully.

evidenceRequirements.artefactType: PDF portfolio/report (dashboard, insights, data dictionary, governance evaluation, recommendations)
evidenceRequirements.additionalNotes: Use the provided report template. Include labelled figures for all charts and a KPI table for the latest month.

evidenceRequirements.fileType: CSV or XLSX; optional PBIX/PQX/JSON for queries or scripts
evidenceRequirements.additionalNotes: Include cleaned dataset(s), calculation sheets, and any transformation queries/scripts. If using the provided dataset, include the KPI checker sheet; auto-marking will verify selected KPI values.

evidenceRequirements.fileType: PDF (plan) and image/PDF exports of screenshots; optional script files
evidenceRequirements.additionalNotes: Plan must specify trigger, refresh steps, commentary template, distribution list, and controls. Include screenshots of schedule/configuration or a reproducible manual refresh SOP.

evidenceRequirements.artefactType: Screen recording: dashboard and automation walkthrough
evidenceRequirements.additionalNotes: If audio is not possible, include on-screen captions and provide a transcript (PDF). Show calculations, dashboard features, and the refresh/distribution process.
Anonymise recipients for submission. Template should include space for headline changes, drivers, and actions.

self_study.academicIntegrity: You must complete the work independently. Use only anonymised or simulated data. You may use the provided templates, vendor documentation, and general software help resources. You may use assistive tools (e.g., spellcheck, grammar check, captioning) and minor formula/debugging help, but all analysis, insights, governance evaluation, and automation design must be your own. Do not share your files with other learners or collaborate on calculations or narrative content. Do not submit work generated by another person or by generative AI without your own critical verification and substantial authorship. Cite any third-party materials used (e.g., definitions, methods) using Harvard style in your PDF. Include the declaration of authenticity in your portfolio: “I confirm that this submission is my own work, that all sources are acknowledged, and that no unauthorised assistance was used.”
self_study.accessibilityOptions: Reasonable adjustments are available without reducing academic standards. Alternatives include: providing a written transcript if audio recording is not possible; submitting additional static screenshots if interactive dashboards cannot be shared; using high-contrast palettes and descriptive alt text/captions for figures; submitting captions for the MP4 or a full transcript; extended time windows where approved. All templates are screen-reader compatible. If a specific tool is not accessible to you, use an equivalent accessible tool and document how you met the same requirements.

brief.studentFacingIntro: In this portfolio you will create a practical HR metrics dashboard, evaluate and improve the underlying data governance, and set up a repeatable automation for monthly reporting. The work mirrors a typical HR operations/reporting cycle and must remain within the confidentiality expectations of HR data. You may complete all tasks fully online or in-person-supported, with options to present live or submit a recording. Collaboration for feedback is encouraged during development, but the final submission must be your own work.
brief.workplaceContext: You are supporting an HR Manager who requires a reliable monthly dashboard for departmental reporting to track turnover, absence, and recruitment pipeline trends. Recent reporting errors and inconsistent definitions have raised concerns about data quality and governance. The HR Manager needs (1) an accurate, explainable dashboard with concise narrative insights for leaders, (2) a clear evaluation of data definitions, sources, and quality with prioritised governance recommendations agreed with stakeholders, and (3) an automated monthly update and distribution process with commentary prompts.
stepByStepInstructions: Confirm data access and confidentiality: Use the provided synthetic HR dataset (or organisation-approved anonymised data). Remove any direct identifiers. Document your data sources.

Define metrics and scope: Specify how you will calculate turnover, absence, and pipeline. State the reporting period(s), population, inclusions/exclusions, and any segmentation (e.g., department, location, tenure).

Prepare and validate data: Clean and structure datasets (e.g., employees, leavers, absences, vacancies/applicants). Check completeness, duplicates, date ranges, and alignment of keys. Keep notes of data quality issues discovered.

Build the dashboard: In a tool of your choice (e.g., Excel, Google Sheets, Power BI, Tableau), design an HR dashboard that clearly highlights turnover, absence, and pipeline trends over time. Include filters where appropriate and ensure labels, definitions, and time frames are visible.
Add narrative insights: Write concise commentary (bullets or short paragraphs) that explains notable trends, variances, and potential drivers, and flags risks or actions for HR/line managers.

Evaluate data definitions, sources, and quality: Create a short data dictionary for key fields and metrics. Identify all data sources and assess quality issues (e.g., timeliness, completeness, accuracy, consistency). Prioritise issues using evidence and impact.

Recommend governance improvements with stakeholders: Propose practical actions (e.g., ownership, definitions, validation checks, change control, retention) and outline a stakeholder engagement plan (e.g., RACI, communications, approvals).

Set up monthly automation: Configure a method to refresh data and update the dashboard monthly (e.g., scheduled data refresh, macro/script, scheduled email distribution). Include commentary prompts/templates and a maintained distribution list.
Test and evidence automation: Run at least one test cycle. Capture screenshots or a short screen recording demonstrating the refresh and distribution steps, and export any scheduler settings/logs.

Quality check and package: Ensure calculations are correct, visuals are readable, commentary is specific and data-backed, and governance recommendations are feasible. Compile your artefacts into the required portfolio structure and submit. If presenting live, book a slot; otherwise include a 5–8 minute recorded walkthrough.
deliverables: HR metrics dashboard file highlighting turnover, absence, and recruitment pipeline trends, with clear labels and definitions.
Narrative insights explaining key trends, anomalies, and implications for action.
Data definitions and quality evaluation including a concise data dictionary, source register, and prioritised quality findings.
Governance improvement recommendations with a stakeholder engagement plan (e.g., RACI, communications, checkpoints).
Automation setup evidence: scheduler/export settings, scripts/macros if used, screenshots or a 5–8 minute screen recording of a test run.
Monthly distribution list and commentary template used for report updates.
Walkthrough presentation: either live (in scheduled session) or a 5–8 minute recorded overview covering dashboard, governance evaluation, and automation.

rubric.criterionName: Dashboard analysis and insights (turnover, absence, pipeline)
rubric.fail: Metrics for one or more required areas (turnover, absence, pipeline) are missing or incorrectly calculated; visuals are unclear or misleading; time frames/labels are inconsistent; commentary is absent or not supported by data.
rubric.pass: Correctly calculates and displays turnover, absence, and pipeline over the defined period with readable visuals and clear labels/definitions; identifies basic trends and provides brief, data-linked commentary.
rubric.merit: Accurate, consistent calculations with well-structured visuals enabling comparison across time and relevant segments; narrative highlights significant trends, anomalies, and plausible drivers with evidence; methods and definitions are transparent.
rubric.distinction: Robust analysis with meaningful segmentation (e.g., department, tenure) and appropriate handling of seasonality or comparability; well-designed, user-friendly dashboard (e.g., filters) that supports decision-making; incisive commentary translates insights into clear actions/risks and evidences reproducibility.

rubric.criterionName: Evaluation of definitions, sources, and data quality; governance recommendations with stakeholders
rubric.fail: Key terms are undefined; data sources are not identified; quality issues are not assessed or are purely descriptive without evidence; recommendations are generic or impractical; stakeholder considerations are missing.
rubric.pass: Defines key metrics/fields; lists data sources; identifies basic quality issues (e.g., completeness, accuracy) with examples; proposes feasible governance improvements; identifies relevant stakeholder roles.
rubric.merit: Critically evaluates strengths and limitations of definitions and sources; prioritises quality risks with evidence (e.g., profiling checks, error rates); proposes practical governance improvements (e.g., ownership, validation controls, change log) with an outline stakeholder plan (e.g., RACI, communications).
rubric.distinction: Provides an evidence-led, comprehensive evaluation using appropriate profiling/triangulation; delivers a feasible, prioritised governance roadmap with risk/impact rationale aligned to data protection expectations; details stakeholder engagement with clear responsibilities, approvals, and measurable success criteria.

rubric.criterionName: Application of report automation and distribution
rubric.fail: No working automation is demonstrated; schedule and distribution are unclear or absent; commentary is not incorporated.
rubric.pass: Implements a basic, working monthly refresh and distribution to a defined list; includes a simple commentary template or process; provides screenshots or a short recording evidencing the setup.
rubric.merit: Implements a reliable, documented automation that refreshes data, updates visuals, and supports commentary capture; includes basic error handling and evidence of a successful test run; distribution is appropriately segmented with handover notes.
rubric.distinction: Delivers a production-ready, secure automation with parameterised refresh, clear version control, monitoring/logs, and rollback steps; schedule accounts for reporting calendars; distribution and permissions align to data protection expectations; evidence includes a successful scheduled run and configuration export.
